questions.a: The region around a magnet where its force can be detected, shown by field lines.

questions.q: How do you map the field of a bar magnet?
questions.a: Sprinkle iron filings or move a compass around it; the needle's direction at many points traces the field lines.

questions.q: Inside a bar magnet, in which direction do field lines run?
questions.a: From the south pole to the north pole, completing the closed loops.

concepts.title: Magnetic Effects of Current - Solenoid and Electromagnet

questions.q: How does a solenoid create a uniform magnetic field?
questions.a: Many circular turns in series add their fields, giving nearly uniform field inside the coil.
A soft iron core inside a current-carrying solenoid; it behaves as a strong magnet only while current flows.

questions.q: State one use of an electromagnet.
questions.a: Lifting heavy iron scrap in cranes, or in electric bells and MRI machines.

concepts.title: Force on a Conductor, Electric Motor and Electromagnetic Induction

questions.a: Production of a current in a closed coil when the magnetic field through it changes - moving a magnet into the coil.
With right-hand fingers at right angles: forefinger along field, thumb along motion of conductor, middle finger gives induced current direction.

questions.q: On what does the induced current in a coil depend?
questions.a: On the rate of change of magnetic field through the coil and the number of turns.
